findings.title: Initialization can be front-run
findings.description: The InitStore instruction initializes a singleton PDA that holds the OApp configuration and registers the OApp with LayerZero, also setting the admin. This instruction can only be invoked once. However, if program deployment and OApp initialization are not performed atomically in the same transaction, the initialization can be front-run by an attacker. The root cause is the lack of atomicity between deployment and initialization, allowing a malicious actor to invoke InitStore first with their own parameters. An attacker could exploit this by monitoring the mempool for deployment transactions and quickly submitting their own InitStore transaction. The impact is that the OApp could be initialized with an incorrect administrator and LayerZero endpoint addresses, rendering the intended deployment invalid and requiring a full redeployment of the program.

findings.title: Ambiguous state initialization
findings.description: Both the Solana and EVM example OApps store received messages in permanent storage, initializing the message variable with the default string "Nothing received yet." This creates ambiguity because the state of a newly initialized OApp is indistinguishable from the state of an OApp that has received a message with that exact content. The root cause is the use of a sentinel value that could also be a legitimate message, rather than using an explicit state indicator. An attacker or malicious sender could send a message with the content "Nothing received yet.", making it impossible for the application or its users to determine whether a message was actually received. While this does not lead to direct fund loss or critical failure in the example context, it sets a poor precedent for real-world applications, potentially leading to logic errors or misinterpretation of state in production implementations.
